title: Evidence of Cognitive Deficits andDevelopmental Advances in Generative AI: A Clock Drawing Test Analysis

live_model.evidence: "The language models we tested (as of July 2024) were ... OpenAI's ... GPT-4 Turbo..." (Sec. 2.1); Table 2 row "GPT-4 Turbo 2 0 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 2 1 1 1 14 4" (Total=14, Weighted=4)

prompt.location: Sec. 2.2 ("draw the face of a clock, put in the numbers, and set the hands to 10 minutes after nine", plus an SVG-rendering instruction for text-only LLMs)
prompt.note: Single fixed prompt, administered once per model with no fine-tuning or repeated sampling.

claim.metric: CDT Weighted Score (WMS-IV BCSE scoring rubric, Wechsler 2009)
claim.location: Table 2, row "GPT-4 Turbo" (Total=14, Weighted=4); Abstract ("Only GPT 4 Turbo and Gemini Pro 1.5 successfully produced the correct time... Weighted score = 4/4")

data.source: Task is fully self-contained (fixed prompt, no external dataset); scoring rubric is the published WMS-IV BCSE (Wechsler, 2009)

notes: Marked 'maybe' because the headline score requires a human rater trained on the WMS-IV BCSE clock-drawing rubric to grade the raw SVG/text output (a well-defined but manual, non-automatic scoring step), and because the design is a single trial per model (n=1, 'once per model... no previous prompting'). GPT-4o (multimodal) is also tested in the same paper; undated but the testing period ('as of July 2024') precedes the 2024-10-02 cutoff, so it would resolve to gpt-4o-2024-05-13 (Table 2 row: Total=9, Weighted=2). The live_ids CSV hint of a dated snapshot was not found verbatim in the text; both GPT-4 Turbo and GPT-4o appear undated, resolved here via the alias/date rules.
